problem_markdown: A circle has centre on side $AB$ of cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ and touches each of $BC,CD,DA$. Prove $AD+BC=AB$.
solutions_markdown:
Let the circle have centre $O$, radius $r$, and contacts $L\in AD$, $M\in CD$, $N\in BC$. Write $\angle A=\alpha$ and $\angle B=\beta$. The right triangles at the tangencies give $AL=r\cot\alpha$, $BN=r\cot\beta$, $AO=r\csc\alpha$, and $BO=r\csc\beta$.

Cyclicity gives $\angle C=\pi-\alpha$ and $\angle D=\pi-\beta$. Since a circle's centre lies on the angle bisector between its two tangents, the other tangent lengths are
$$CN=CM=r\cot(\angle C/2)=r\tan(\alpha/2),$$
$$DL=DM=r\tan(\beta/2).$$
Using $\cot t+\tan(t/2)=\csc t$, we obtain
$$AD+BC=(AL+LD)+(BN+NC)=r(\csc\alpha+\csc\beta)=AO+OB=AB.$$
